title: Match reasoning narrates over pre-computed deterministic facts (full profile + real JD + score breakdown), not free-form
expected: Reasoning bound to THIS candidate's real CV and THIS real JD, grounded in deterministic match facts.
got: Client sends only an ID ref; server resolves the FULL profile (match-input.ts:32-44) and hands the LIVE DB corpus to the CLI via --jobs-json (match/route.ts:47-52) so an ingested job ranks against its real record. The reasoning prompt receives the real candidate skills, real job must-haves, and the pre-computed match (matched/missing skills + dimension scores) — match_reasoning.py:34-75 — so the LLM narrates over deterministic facts rather than inventing a match. Verdict/strengths/gaps/interviewProbes structure.
l2_priority: Run a real CS role + candidate; assert the verdict names skills from THIS CV and gaps tied to THIS JD's must-haves — generic boilerplate = senior-quality quality-gap.
suggested_acceptance: Reasoning cites >=1 concrete fact from the candidate's CV and references the role; no two candidates share interchangeable boilerplate.

title: Template-vs-AI degrade is honestly disclosed with a 'Rule-based' badge (cs: 'pravidlové')
expected: When the deterministic template is served (allowance exhausted / no key / provider outage), the user must know it's not AI-reasoned.
got: Past the ai_candidates allowance — the same path a missing key/outage takes — reasoning-run.ts:63 pushes --no-llm and the deterministic template stays uncached (reasoning-cache-policy.ts). MatchShared.tsx:73-76 renders a source badge: source==='llm' -> 'LLM' else 'pravidlové' (cs.json:2018-2019), plus a '· z mezipaměti' cached suffix. The provenance is in plain sight, not hidden.
l2_priority: Confirm the badge actually renders cs 'pravidlové' on a keyless/over-allowance run and that the deterministic verdict is structurally coherent.
suggested_acceptance: Every reasoning panel shows an AI-vs-rule-based provenance badge; the template path is never presented as AI-reasoned.

title: Score comes with drivers, not a bare number — per-dimension contribution+weight breakdown + confidence-band 'why'
expected: If it says 78%, show the three things that made it 78 and the one thing that capped it (Petra's 'what good looks like').
got: ScoreBreakdown (MatchShared.tsx:152-198) renders each dimension's contribution width + percent + weight, all server-supplied. Confidence band surfaces its drivers inline when not tight (MatchCard.tsx:167-171, 'Proč toto rozpětí'). Partial taxonomy matches are marked '~' so 'matched: Kubernetes' is not read as verified possession (MatchCard.tsx:186-194); provenance labels on early-career skills.
l2_priority: Kateřina's lens carries here: confirm the breakdown numbers are legible/calibratable live, not just decorative bars.
suggested_acceptance: Any match score is accompanied by its per-dimension drivers (raised/capped), not a bare number.

title: Jobs-side candidate-scan empty state is a hardcoded English string for a Czech recruiter
expected: Czech UI throughout; an English headline string is a language finding (Petra's scored criterion).
got: app/api/jobs/[id]/candidates/route.ts:~22 returns note:'No saved candidates yet.' as a raw English literal (no t()), so Petra sees English when the pool is empty. The Match tab's own empty state IS i18n'd (ChainEmptyState); this is the Jobs->candidates scan path only.
l2_priority: Confirm the string surfaces in the UI (not swallowed) on an empty pool in a cs session.
suggested_acceptance: All recruiter-facing empty-state copy renders via next-intl in cs.

title: Reasoning prompt omits the role's salary band even though the card shows it
expected: A defensible 'why these three' could reference comp fit; the salary_band is on the MatchResult.
got: match_reasoning.py reasoning_context() builds candidate+job+match facts but does NOT include job.salary_band; the band is on MatchResult (matching.py) and rendered on the card (MatchCard.tsx:147) but never reaches the narrative prompt. Minor — comp grounding lives in the Analyze salary gauge, and the card shows the band; the reasoning just can't speak to comp fit.
l2_priority: Low priority — confirm whether comp-fit ever appears in a verdict; if Petra expects it, raise severity.
suggested_acceptance: Where comp fit matters, the reasoning can reference the role band; otherwise the card band is sufficient.

title: Shortlist completion depends on a seeded candidate pool fixture
expected: From an open/ingested JD she reaches a ranked shortlist without a dead-end.
got: buildCandidatePool() combines v2 profiles (cap 100) + CV analyses (cap 60); with none seeded the Jobs scan returns the empty note and the Match tab shows ChainEmptyState. Structurally sound but gated on the fixture (env.md seed_pipeline/seed_candidates + seeded analyses). Tag for L2 reachability confirmation.
l2_priority: Reachability: confirm the ČS seed produces a non-empty pool so a real role ranks candidates live.
suggested_acceptance: With the canonical seed loaded, an open ČS role returns a ranked, non-empty shortlist.

title: Salary gauge is anchored in a sourced role-band benchmark with a stated basis, not a naked LLM number
expected: A salary figure must carry a basis (band/seniority/market) — a bare number is worthless to Petra.
got: data/salary_benchmarks.json holds role x seniority CZK/month bands with cited sources (Platy.cz, Kitalent, expats.cz, Glassdoor). The prompt instructs Gemini to use the deterministic anchor_band as primary anchor, adjust only +/-20% with evidence, and cite the anchor in salary.rationale (gemini.py:~422-445). SalaryTab.tsx:43,62-63 renders a confidence badge + rationale bullets; company-context multiplier and grounded market evidence shown when present.
l2_priority: Read a live result: assert the salary number cites a band/benchmark in the rationale (not vibes) and the confidence badge reflects grounding state.
suggested_acceptance: Every salary estimate shows its basis (anchor band + adjustment + confidence), never a naked amount.

title: Headline job-fit matched/missing skill chips are pure LLM lists with no deterministic taxonomy gate (hallucination seam)
expected: Every named skill traceable to the source CV; zero hallucinated skills (Petra: one fabrication = blocker).
got: job_fit.matching_skills / missing_skills come straight from Gemini (pipeline.py:~624; gemini.py:98-112) with NO taxonomy matcher enforcing that a 'matched' skill exists in the CV — so the LLM CAN list a skill the CV never mentions. A separate DETERMINISTIC keyword-coverage check (ats.py:35-78) runs in parallel and is shown alongside (JobFitTab.tsx KeywordCoverage), which mitigates but does not gate the headline SkillChips. Petra's exact pet peeve lives in this seam.
l2_priority: ADVERSARIAL: run a real CV+JD and verify every 'matched' chip is findable in the CV text; any invented skill is a blocker for Petra. Check whether SkillChips visually distinguishes deterministic-verified from LLM-asserted skills.
suggested_acceptance: A 'matched' skill is either cross-checked against the CV/keyword-coverage or visibly marked as LLM-asserted vs CV-verified; no unqualified hallucinated skill in the headline chips.

title: Job-fit verdict is generated against the supplied JD (must_prove_evidence), or nulled when no JD is given
expected: Job-fit against THIS role, not a generic rubric.
got: The route carries the real JD (text/file/jdSlug) + company overview + grounding flag into the Python run; gemini.py:389-393 nulls job_fit when no JD is supplied and populates it fully against the JD when present; must_prove_evidence surfaces in JobFitTab.tsx:62-68. Full CV + real JD reach the pipeline (analyze-run.ts cliArgs --job-description-path/-text), JD content is in the cache key so different JDs never collide.
l2_priority: Assert the live verdict references the JD's must-haves; re-run same CV with cs<->en report-language and confirm narrative language + cache-correctness.
suggested_acceptance: The verdict references the JD's must-haves; with no JD, job-fit is honestly absent rather than a generic rubric.

title: Report-language override flows end-to-end to the prompt and is language-keyed in cache
expected: Czech narrative for a Czech recruiter; an English-only headline is a finding.
got: AnalyzeForm report-language select (AnalyzeForm.tsx:212-223) -> route lang -> CLI --lang -> gemini.py output_language instruction forcing every freeform field into the chosen language; lang is part of computeCacheKey (analyze-run.ts) so re-running cs vs en is cache-correct. Code values/skills stay verbatim by design.
l2_priority: Confirm a cs run returns a genuinely Czech narrative (no English leakage) and an en override on the same CV returns English without a stale cache hit.
suggested_acceptance: The generated narrative renders in the selected report language end-to-end.

title: Candidate drawer timeline genuinely merges 5 cross-surface event sources + stage events into one chronological feed
expected: Open the drawer and see the candidate's WHOLE history in one place, no silent state loss.
got: candidate-timeline.ts:38-80 merges analyses, interview created/completed, schedule invites sent/confirmed, offers extended/responded, and comms into one time-sorted feed; the drawer adds pipeline stage events from the events stream (CandidateDrawer.tsx:234-258). Honest caveat the code flags itself: analyses are joined by exact case-insensitive candidate label (no fuzzy join that would invent history for same-named strangers).
l2_priority: Open a candidate with history; spot-check that a scheduled interview AND a prior analysis both appear in chronological order.
suggested_acceptance: The drawer shows a unified chronological feed across analysis/decision/comms/schedule/offer, not just stage changes.

title: Stage moves are optimistic-concurrency guarded (expectedStage CAS + IMMEDIATE transaction) — no silent revert/clobber
expected: A move sticks; a stale-tab move can't silently clobber a concurrent change.
got: Drag and drawer moves send expectedStage (PipelineTab.tsx:506; CandidateDrawer.tsx:316); actOnPipelineEntry checks row.stage===expectedStage under an IMMEDIATE lock (db/pipeline.ts:1232-1237,1326) and the route returns 409 with the fresh entry on a lost CAS. The NL command bar previews before mutating and reuses the SAME guarded action (command/route.ts:61-86).
l2_priority: Drag forward, refresh, confirm persistence; drag back and confirm both moves recorded (no silent loss).
suggested_acceptance: A concurrent stale-tab move is refused with a clear 409, never silently overwriting the newer state.

title: A plain drag/manual stage move closes the drawer and reloads the board with NO explicit confirmation toast
expected: After every action she sees an explicit confirmation of what happened and to whom — no silent success ('a stalo se vubec neco?').
got: moveStage() calls postPipelineAction then onChanged()+onClose() (CandidateDrawer.tsx:311-325) — the drawer closes and the board reloads, but there is no toast/badge stating 'Moved <candidate> to <stage>'. By contrast AI automation actions DO show a colored outcome badge (CandidateResultView). The move IS reflected on the board reload so it is not fully silent, but it lacks the explicit who/what confirmation Petra's criterion calls for.
l2_priority: Confirm live whether the board change is salient enough on reload, or whether the absence of a 'moved to X' toast reads as silent success to Petra.
suggested_acceptance: A successful stage move shows an explicit confirmation of which candidate moved to which stage.

title: Advancing to interview/offer reaches a real next-step (mint voice/schedule link, extend offer) from the drawer
expected: Advancing to interview/offer is one obvious action; the hand-off isn't a dead-end.
got: For Screened/Interview entries the drawer exposes voice-screen link minting (/api/interview/create) and schedule-invite minting (/api/schedule/invite) (CandidateDrawer.tsx:845-852,911-918); an Offer-stage accept routes through extendOffer() which mints+dispatches the tokenized offer (pipeline/[id]/route.ts:22-68). Next steps are two-step (move then mint) rather than a single drawer button.
l2_priority: Confirm the mint affordances are reachable from the drawer for a real entry and produce working tokens.
suggested_acceptance: From the drawer, an advanced candidate can reach interview/schedule/offer hand-offs without a dead-end.

title: Voice screen is consent-gated server-side, single-use, and denial-of-wallet guarded; transcript+result land on the entry
expected: A human still decides; she gets a transcript + usable result attached to the right pipeline entry, same language.
got: connect/route.ts enforces consent server-side (isConnectConsentSatisfied, 137-139, 403 without consent), refuses bad/absent tokens before minting credentials (56-61), and 409s a completed/revoked/expired/terminal session (70-72,83-98). Candidate sessions carry grounded instructions; a tokenless lab session falls to generic defaults (117-119,148-151). Petra reviews via /api/interview/by-entry -> InterviewTranscriptModal (transcript turns + AI scorecard + recommendation), language stored verbatim; the interview produces a transcript+result, NOT an auto-advance (human decides).
l2_priority: Run a REAL candidate-token session; assert questions reference this role/candidate and the transcript+scorecard land on Petra's entry in cs.
suggested_acceptance: A completed screen attaches a transcript + result to the correct entry in the same language; consent is enforced before any credential is minted.

title: Candidate interview grounding is analysis-derived (JD must-haves + analysis signals), not full-CV or comp-band
expected: The agent should ask questions grounded in THIS candidate and THIS role.
got: buildGroundedInstructions (interview/grounding.ts) assembles the candidate session from the pipeline entry's analysis + job record — JD must-haves, screening focus, prior analysis signals — but NOT the full CV text or the comp band. Adequate for a first-round screen and clearly better than the generic lab default, but the grounding is a summary, not the full CV.
l2_priority: Listen to a live grounded session: do the questions feel specific to this candidate's CV, or only to the JD/analysis summary? If generic, raise to major.
suggested_acceptance: The candidate-mode interview references specifics from this candidate's evidence, not just the role title.

title: Petra's voice-screen review depends on a completed real-token session fixture + a voice key
expected: She sends the screen and gets back a transcript+result.
got: The candidate side (/interview/[token]) is Tereza's tokenized surface; Petra's review (InterviewTranscriptModal via /api/interview/by-entry) needs a completed session for the entry, which needs a minted interview token (env.md fixture #5) and an OpenAI Realtime/ElevenLabs key. Keyless connect 503s with a 'set KEY in .env.local' message. Structurally sound; reachability of the END-TO-END loop is an L2/fixture question.
l2_priority: Confirm the token-mint path produces a session /connect accepts and that a completed session surfaces a transcript on Petra's entry.
suggested_acceptance: With a voice key + minted token, a completed screen yields a transcript+scorecard on Petra's entry.

title: Candidate offer-accept card is a 'People team will be in touch' thank-you with NO link to the onboarding next-step
expected: Accept lands on a concrete onboarding next-step (the /onboarding/[token] questionnaire), not a dead-end thank-you — the explicit goal of this journey and of commits 59f55c3 / the offers work.
got: OfferView type has NO onboarding token/URL field; the accepted-state card (offer/[token]/page.tsx:194-200) renders only acceptedTitle + acceptedBodyCompany, which in cs.json:486 reads 'Vitejte ... Nas personalni tym se vam brzy ozve s podrobnostmi k nastupu' — literally the old dead-end the work was meant to remove. The /onboarding/[token] page EXISTS and is wired server-side (accept -> Hired + onboarding dispatch), but the candidate-facing offer page does NOT surface an onward link/button to it. Tagged unreachable for Petra: this is Tereza's tokenized surface (outside Petra's binding); Petra's own hand-off (OnboardingTab) DOES receive the hired candidate + their answers, so her job is not blocked — but the journey's central promise fails on the candidate leg.
l2_priority: Accept a REAL offer token live and confirm whether ANY onward onboarding link is rendered; if the accepted card is a bare thank-you, the dead-end fix did not land on the candidate page. (Reachability: this is Tereza's surface, not Petra's — confirm Petra's OnboardingTab receives the hired candidate regardless.)
suggested_acceptance: On accept, the candidate sees a clickable next-step into the onboarding questionnaire (mint + link the onboarding token), not just 'we'll be in touch'.

title: Petra's offer->onboarding hand-off round-trips: draft/send from Decisions, watch Hired in OnboardingTab, candidate answers surface back
expected: Draft the offer with the right comp, send a clean link, watch it move to accepted without re-keying; the candidate's answers reach her.
got: Offer drafted/sent from the Decisions queue (AiReviewCard 'Send offer' -> /api/pipeline/[id] accept -> extendOffer dispatches the tokenized link with the REAL persisted salary/currency, not a placeholder). OnboardingTab pulls /api/onboarding to list hired candidates + runs with progress; RunDetailView auto-fills the pre-boarding questionnaire from the candidate's submitted intake (OnboardingTab.tsx:167-168,240-241). The e-signature step is honestly flagged as a 'provider seam' (amber note) rather than faked.
l2_priority: End-to-end: send a real offer, accept it, submit the questionnaire, confirm the answers appear in Petra's OnboardingTab run detail.
suggested_acceptance: Petra can send an offer with real comp and see the accepted candidate + their submitted answers on her hand-off tab without re-keying.

title: No proactive 'offer accepted' signal — Petra infers acceptance from the stage move / OnboardingTab
expected: Watch it move to accepted (clarity of what happened and to whom).
got: Accept transitions the entry to Hired and queues onboarding server-side, but there is no push/notification to Petra; she discovers it by the candidate appearing in OnboardingTab's hired list or by the pipeline stage. Acceptable, but it leans on her checking rather than telling her.
l2_priority: Confirm whether an accepted offer surfaces an attention badge/notification anywhere Petra naturally looks.
suggested_acceptance: An accepted offer produces a visible signal (badge/notification) on a surface Petra monitors.

title: The simulation drives REAL surfaces (opens the actual /offer/[token] to click Accept), keyless, and is isolated from tenant data
expected: Show a stakeholder what the tool does in two minutes without exposing candidate data or burning AI credits; it must feel real, not a video.
got: The Hired step opens the real /offer/[token] in an iframe and clicks the actual offer-accept button (SimulationProvider.tsx:585-605, with an API fallback), driving a real transition. The walk is keyless: canned JD from the company template, deterministic screen/offer drafts (no LLM). Isolation is marker-based: every sim artifact is titled '(SIM)' and resetSim() deletes only rows matching that marker (sim-store.ts), so seeded tenant candidates are never mutated.
l2_priority: Run keyless end-to-end with NO auth/keys; assert the offer step truly opens /offer/[token] and the run never surfaces/mutates real seeded candidates.
suggested_acceptance: The keyless run traverses real surfaces (real offer accept) and leaves zero tenant residue.
